summary: INVESTIGATION run for Quote SA-260604-165816 (Apex Display Group / 30 Ct. Jerky, ZIP 19446, Multi-Part Matched Set, 3 components × 2 set qtys 100/150). Logged in as admin, loaded the quote from Team Saved Quotes, opened Freight Dashboard, ran Update All Rates (~85s for 8 UTS quotes), then captured Per Item and Per Job views, the comparison banner, the Allocate-by toolbar, and the right-side Quote Table freight column. All requested numeric values are captured below in test_results. NO pass/fail judgments — observation only. Two SCREENSHOTS saved: /app/test_reports/dash_per_item.png and /app/test_reports/dash_per_job.png. Note: the closing right-panel 'Item Freight' card was not in view after Per Job switch (the dashboard's Per Job toggle changed the right-side Type to Per Job, which collapses the per-item card into the per-job card).

02_dashboard_initial.note: Cache was already populated from a prior run, so banner numbers were present before the click. After Update All Rates the same values were re-rendered (cache refresh, no change).

03_per_item_view_AFTER_update.observation: EVERY component row in BOTH qty sections shows IDENTICAL freight ($161.56 raw / $185.79 w/markup), even though total weights, skid sizes, and footprints differ significantly across components (Display Base 244/316 lbs, 1L skid 5ft vs Header 109/125 lbs, 1S skid 4ft). Section Raw totals are identical too ($484.68 = 3 × $161.56) for BOTH qty 100 and qty 150 — qty 150 has 148 lbs more product weight but produces the same per-item freight totals. This matches the user-reported symptom 'freight is not being applied per item correctly'.

04_per_job_view.observation: Per-Job correctly differentiates by qty (Qty 100 raw $161.56 vs Qty 150 raw $200.56) and produces sensible weight-proportional allocations across components. wt% sums to 100.0% in both scenarios. This view appears internally consistent.

05_quote_table_after_dashboard_close.observation: After clicking the dashboard's green 'Per Job' button (in the Recommendation banner), the right-side Freight panel switched from 'Per Item' to 'Per Job' mode (the right panel header read 'PER-JOB FREIGHT $1,521.50 · Allocated by MSF across 3 components' in the final screenshot). The Quote Table freight column then read $185.79 for BOTH qty rows. NOTE: Before opening the dashboard, the freight footer read 'QTY 100 Items: $3,964.32 Freight: $557.38' and the right-side Item Freight card read 'ITEM 1 · FREIGHT · QTY 100  $185.79  ($161.56 + 15% markup)' (i.e. per-component, not per-set). The Quote Table FREIGHT column at that pre-dashboard moment read $557.38 for BOTH the qty 100 and qty 150 rows — same number for two different set quantities.

test_results.06_item_freight_card_at_end: Not captured directly — after the Per Job switch the right-side panel rendered the Per-Job freight card instead of the per-item card. The Per-Job card showed 'PER-JOB FREIGHT $1,521.50' with subtitle '$161.56 + 15% markup · Allocated by MSF across 3 components'. The dashboard 'Type: Per Job' toggle had been engaged.

key_findings_for_diagnosis: Per-Item dashboard: ALL component rows show the SAME freight ($161.56 raw / $185.79 w/markup) for BOTH qty 100 and qty 150 — independent of component weight, skid size, footprint, or set qty. This is the user-reported defect.
Per-Item section RAW totals are identical for qty 100 and qty 150 ($484.68 each), even though qty 150 has +148 lbs more total weight. Per-Item view is NOT differentiating by qty either.
Per-Job view DOES correctly differentiate: Qty 100 = $161.56 (548 lbs), Qty 150 = $200.56 (696 lbs). Weight-proportional component allocation in Per-Job looks correct (wt% sums to 100%).

Pre-dashboard Quote Table FREIGHT column showed $557.38 for BOTH qty rows (= 3 × $185.79 component freight); after switching to Per Job mode it showed $185.79 for BOTH qty rows (also identical across qtys — should be $185.79 for qty 100 vs $230.64 for qty 150 if per-qty allocation were live).

Hypothesis (for main agent): in RightDashboard.jsx updateFreight() MP branch (L375-515), the perItemMap appears to be built from a single per-component UTS quote rather than firing one UTS quote per (component × qty) slot. The values $161.56 / $185.79 are exactly the Per-Job qty-100 carrier rate ($161.56) — suggesting the per-item path is reusing the qty-100 combined-job rate as each component's per-item rate, not running independent solo-component quotes. Compare to the qty-150 per-job rate ($200.56) which IS distinct, indicating qty differentiation works on the per-job path but is lost on the per-item path.

Also: the right-side Quote Table FREIGHT column appears to read from a single scalar (state.freightCost or similar) rather than from freightByQty[slot], so both qty rows render the same number both before and after switching freight type — this is a separate but related quote-table binding issue.
action_items: FIX (HIGH): In RightDashboard.jsx updateFreight() MP branch, ensure perItemMap is built by firing a separate solo UTS quote for EACH (component, qty) slot (expect 6 quotes total for 3 components × 2 qtys), not by reusing the combined Per-Job rate as each component's solo rate. Currently every Per-Item row collapses to the same $161.56 value.

FIX (HIGH): Quote Table FREIGHT column must read per-row from freightByQty[slot] (matching the Item Freight card binding fixed in iteration_35/36), not from a scalar. Both qty 100 and qty 150 rows currently show the same freight before AND after switching Per Item/Per Job.
VERIFY: Per-Job allocation (Qty 100 = $161.56 / Qty 150 = $200.56) is already correct — preserve this when fixing Per-Item.

VERIFY: backend engine/runner.py build_prod_inputs freightByQty per-slot lookup was recently fixed for string keys — confirm the perItemMap keys produced by the frontend match the slot keys the backend expects after the fix.
critical_code_review_comments: RightDashboard.jsx updateFreight() MP branch (L375-515) — the perItemMap construction needs to be audited: it appears to iterate components but not (component × qty), OR it's overwriting per-qty entries with a single value. The fact that qty 100 and qty 150 produce identical Per-Item totals ($484.68 each) is the smoking gun.

FreightDashModal.jsx PerItemTable L321 — renders directly from state.freightDashCache; the data shape coming in already has identical $161.56 values across slots, so the bug is upstream in the cache builder, not the renderer.
Recommend logging the perItemMap and freightByQty objects in updateFreight() right before commit so the next investigation iteration can see exactly what slot keys are being written.

rca of the issue: Reproduction: 1) Login admin / open Team-saved SA-260604-165816 / open Freight Dashboard / Update All Rates / view Per Item. 2) Observe identical $161.56 raw / $185.79 w/markup on all 3 components in BOTH qty 100 and qty 150 sections; Per-Item section raw total $484.68 = 3 × $161.56 in BOTH sections. Expected: each (component × qty) should produce its own UTS-quoted solo-shipment rate that varies by total weight (244/195/109 lbs at qty 100, 316/255/125 lbs at qty 150) and skid size (1L vs 1S). Root cause (hypothesis, awaits main-agent code dive): RightDashboard.jsx updateFreight() MP branch is not firing independent per-component-per-qty solo UTS quotes; instead each Per-Item slot is being populated with the qty-100 combined Per-Job rate ($161.56), then copied across components and qtys. Per-Job code path uses a different (correct) UTS call sequence which is why it shows distinct qty-100 vs qty-150 totals. Mitigation: rebuild perItemMap with 2 nested loops (components × slotQtys) firing one UTS quote per pair, key results by `${slotIdx}:${componentIdx}` (or compatible string key the backend runner accepts), then render PerItemTable from that map. Separately, fix the Quote Table FREIGHT column to read freightByQty[slot] per row instead of a scalar so qty 100 and qty 150 rows display their own values.
